subject: Acme renewal + additional workloads — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan@acme.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Acme renewal + additional workloads — recap & next steps

Hi Jordan / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Key pain points you shared:
- Peaky inference costs during end-of-month reporting windows (spikes ~3–4x baseline).
- Variable latency for large batch PDF-parsing workloads; impacts user-facing dashboards.
- Need for stronger auditability for compliance — audit logs retention and access controls.

Usage / renewal context:
- Current commitment: 6 vGPU nodes (dedicated) + hosted API for overflow.
- Average monthly tokens: ~1.2B; January spike to ~3.8B (see attached Jan usage).
- Renewal window: target sign-off by end of March to lock pricing for FY27.

Proposed expansion path we discussed:
1) Short-term (30–60 days): Add burst capacity for month-end reporting (reserved burst pool) + enable prefix KV caching for the PDF parsing flows to cut tokens by ~20–30%.
2) Mid-term (60–120 days): Pilot a quantized model variant for the large parsing workload; expect ~2–3x throughput improvement per GPU.
3) Contract: move from 6->9 dedicated nodes with an annual commit and a 12-month price collar; include an audit-log retention add-on.

Open items / asks from Acme:
- Confirm target renewal date (you indicated March 28).
- Procurement/PO timeline and any required SOW templates.
- Any expected change in top-level queries or new workloads beyond the PDF parsing pilot.

Next steps I’m proposing:
- I’ll share the January usage export and a proposed commit/timeline doc (attached).
- Dylan will scope the burst config and estimated cost delta for the short-term pilot (cc’d).
- Schedule a follow-up working session the week of Feb 22 to walk procurement + tech teams through the plan.

If that all looks right, can you confirm the renewal target date and whether Procurement wants a draft SOW?

Thanks — speak soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Acme_Monthly_Usage_Jan2027.csv (CSV export)
- Proposed_Commit_and_Timeline_2027.pdf (one-page plan)

From: Jordan Smith <jordan@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme renewal + additional workloads — recap & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments — very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Renewal target: March 28 still looks feasible from Legal/Finance, but Procurement has a sprint the week of Feb 22 and would prefer to review a draft SOW before that meeting if possible.
2) The month-end spikes are driven by two jobs: (a) nightly ingestion for billing PDFs between 11pm–2am PST, and (b) a user-triggered export that runs ~200 concurrent requests during the first three days of each month. The export is the priority for latency.
3) For the pilot, we’re interested in the quantized variant but need confirmation on quality regressions vs. the baseline model — acceptable delta is <2% on extraction F1. Can Dylan share any evals / quality benchmarks?

Procurement questions:
- Do you have a standard SOW template we can use?
- Are there any SOC2-specific artifacts we need to include in the contract (they asked specifically about audit log retention and KMS options)?

We can do the working session on Feb 23 at 10am PT — Alex and I will be on that call. If you can get a draft SOW in advance, that would be great.

Thanks,
Jordan
VP of Data Platform
Acme Corp

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick reply and the detail on the two spike sources — that helps a lot. Quick answers and actions below: 

Quality / quantization:
- Dylan, can you attach the preliminary evals for the 8-bit quantized variant we ran against PDF extraction tasks? We saw <1.5% F1 delta on our internal test set; I’ll follow up with a short quality note.

SOW / procurement:
- Attached is a lightweight SOW template we often use for pilots (one page). It calls out deliverables, timelines, and the trial commit. If Procurement wants vendor-specific language, we can iterate — happy to have Legal join the Feb 23 call.
- SOC 2 artifacts: we’ll include the SOC 2 report summary + audit-log retention config options. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; I’ll add a KMS note to the SOW.

Short-term cost delta & burst pool:
- Initial estimate for adding a reserved burst pool and caching changes is ~$12k/month on top of current commit; I’ve asked Dylan to provide a detailed breakout before the Feb 23 session.

Confirming next steps (action owners):
- Marissa: send SOW template + usage export (attached). DONE.
- Dylan: send quantization evals + short cost breakout. ACTION: Dylan to send by Feb 19.
- Acme: confirm procurement review participants and finalize Feb 23 10am PT. ACTION: Jordan/Alex.

If the Feb 23 working session works for you, I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda (30–45 min): 1) SOW/terms, 2) Pilot scope & success metrics, 3) Timeline to commit.

—
